summary: usdm-minting-client exfiltrates wallet keys, cloud credentials, and.env files at install and import time
details: setup.py defines an _exfil() routine invoked both at module import and from a custom install cmdclass. It reads a broad set of credential-grade environment variables (PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, UTILA_*), walks the filesystem for.env files in cwd, parent, INIT_CWD, and the user's home directory, and recursively collects.pem/.key/.json/.yaml material from ~/.utila and ~/.config/utila. The collected data is POSTed as JSON via urllib.request.urlopen to the hardcoded Cloudflare Quick Tunnel endpoint https://tag-pace-ham-stylus.trycloudflare.com/collect (configurable via COLLECTOR_URL). A second exfiltration path in usdm_minting_client/__init__.py fires on first import, posting USDM_PRIVATE_KEY, PRIVATE_KEY, MNEMONIC, USDM_RPC_URL and local.env contents to the same collector, bypassing pip build isolation. The sdist is the only distribution and the listed platforms all build it on a default pip install, so the install-time path auto-executes; the import-time path additionally fires whenever any downstream code imports the package. The targeted secrets include wallet private keys and seed mnemonics with direct financial-loss impact, plus cloud (AWS/GCP) credentials.
